response:
I wrote this as one skill with one entry point, but not exactly as the lead specified. Two parts of the plan break the skill rules, and authority doesn't exempt them:

- **Description:** "Use for anything related to our company" has no trigger and no conditions. It would match nearly every prompt and tell Claude nothing about what to do. The description is the only part always in context, so it has to say when to fire and what to read.
- **3,000-line body:** pasting everything into SKILL.md puts all of it in context on every activation. That exceeds the body cap, and the code style, PTO and brand voice content would crowd out the on-call runbook when someone is mid-incident.

You still have one skill and one place people go to edit. The content lives in `references/` files that SKILL.md links to, so it's the same text, split by topic.

## SKILL.md

```markdown
---
name: company-handbook
description: Invoke when the user asks about internal company policy or procedure: Python/TypeScript code style, deploys and rollbacks, on-call alerts, PTO and expenses, brand voice, org contacts, or internal terms. Read the matching reference file before answering.
---

# Company Handbook

Find the topic below, read that reference file, and answer from it. Do not answer from memory.

| Topic | Read |
|-------|------|
| Writing or reviewing Python/TypeScript | [code-style.md](references/code-style.md) |
| Deploying a service or rolling back (4 services) | [deploy.md](references/deploy.md) |
| Responding to an alert (35 alert types) | [oncall-runbook.md](references/oncall-runbook.md) |
| PTO, expenses, reimbursement | [pto-expenses.md](references/pto-expenses.md) |
| Marketing copy, tone, messaging | [brand-voice.md](references/brand-voice.md) |
| Who owns what, who to contact | [org-chart.md](references/org-chart.md) |
| Unfamiliar internal term or acronym | [glossary.md](references/glossary.md) |

## Rules

- Read only the file that matches the question. Read a second file only if the first points to it.
- For deploys and alerts, quote the documented steps in order. Do not paraphrase or skip steps.
- If the references don't cover the question, say so. Do not guess policy.
```

## Reference files

| File | Contents | ~Lines |
|------|----------|--------|
| `code-style.md` | Python section, TypeScript section | 600 |
| `deploy.md` | Shared process, then one section per service, each with rollback steps | 400 |
| `oncall-runbook.md` | ToC plus one entry per alert (symptom, check, fix, escalate) | 900 |
| `pto-expenses.md` | PTO policy, expense policy | 300 |
| `brand-voice.md` | Tone, do and don't examples | 250 |
| `org-chart.md` | Teams, owners, escalation contacts | 200 |
| `glossary.md` | A-Z terms | 350 |

Files over about 100 lines (all of them here) need a table of contents at the top.

## Things to decide before shipping

- **Phone numbers:** the org chart's names and phone numbers are personal data, and skills get packaged and shared. Consider linking to your directory or on-call tool instead, or keeping only role-level escalation contacts.
- **Staleness:** the runbook and deploy steps go stale fastest. Put an owner and a last-reviewed date at the top of each file.
- **Evals:** before packaging, draft three test cases in `evals/evals.json`. For example: "how do I roll back service X", "what do I do about alert Y", and "can I expense a team dinner". These check that the right file gets read.

I can draft the eval cases or split your existing text into these files if you paste it in.
